items.title: Keke Palmer photographed in sheer Gucci crop top and skirt on Instagram

items.title: Milan Fashion Week SS27 provisional schedule confirms Gucci's Demna-era second collection on Sept 22
items.summary: Trade/lifestyle outlet's updated schedule piece confirms Gucci returns to the Milan runway during Sept 22-28 fashion week, marking creative director Demna's second collection for the house after his February debut -- framed as one of the season's most closely watched shows alongside Fendi's Maria Grazia Chiuri and Marni's Meryll Rogge. Forward-looking anticipation coverage ahead of the actual show later this week.

items.title: Kering shares surged 15% as Gucci Q2 sales beat estimates on US handbag demand
items.summary: Trade press reports Kering shares jumped as much as 15% after Gucci's Q2 2026 sales beat market expectations, driven by stronger-than-forecast US demand for new handbag styles under Demna, with CEO Luca de Meo calling the recovery 'early, fragile, but real.' Older story (late July) resurfaced/still-cited in current turnaround commentary; included as background financial context for Gucci's ongoing ReconKering reset, flagged as outside the 14-day freshness window and not counted toward buzz recency.

items.title: Gucci cuts prices on carry-over styles up to 20-40% under De Meo's repositioning strategy
items.summary: Italian fashion trade outlet reports Gucci has quietly reduced prices on carry-over items -- sneakers from EUR800 to EUR560-595, a polo from EUR650 to EUR455, some bags down as much as 40% -- CEO Luca de Meo acknowledging Kering 'had pushed prices a little too high' and that recent years' increases are 'no longer feasible.' Strategy targets stabilizing average pricing at EUR2,000-3,000. Critical-angle-adjacent story (implicit admission of prior overpricing) resurfaced in ongoing pricing-strategy discourse; outside 14-day freshness window, included as relevant background context only.

items.summary: Active collector-community thread with members reporting stitching coming apart on purse straps, tarnishing of the G-symbol hardware and zipper pulls, and a zipper breaking after a single use on recently purchased pieces; some posters counter that quality holds up fine with proper care and note responsive refund service. items.title: Gucci secondhand sales rise on resale platforms even as new-product sales decline
items.summary: European luxury trade outlet reports Gucci was the best-selling luxury label on Vestiaire Collective by volume, with legacy Tom Ford-era pieces (Jordaan loafers, archive bags) continuing to hold resale value while new-collection items sell at steep discounts (30-70% off retail) secondhand, framed as a signal that demand for Gucci as heritage/archive is outpacing appetite for current-season product. Critical-angle secondary-market signal included per anti-bias mandate; outside 14-day window, included as relevant recurring context.

items.title: Gucci's AI-generated pre-show Instagram campaign draws 'AI slop' criticism ahead of Demna debut
items.summary: Industry commentary outlet analyzes the backlash after Gucci flooded its Instagram grid with AI-generated images (a satellite, a horse on a beach, a stylized sports car, a woman in a fur coat) tagged 'created with AI' ahead of Demna's runway debut, with critics arguing a house charging upward of $850 for handbags has little credibility cutting corners with synthetic imagery in place of human models and photographers. Foundational critical-angle story on Gucci's AI strategy still actively cited in ongoing commentary around this week's second Demna show; original publish date outside 14-day window, included as necessary context still shaping current discourse (see companion CNN piece).

items.title: Can Gucci make luxury AI? CNN examines the brand's AI-content strategy and backlash
items.summary: T1 wire/broadcast outlet examines whether a heritage luxury house can credibly deploy AI-generated imagery in its marketing without undermining its craftsmanship narrative, situating Gucci's pre-show AI campaign within a wider industry debate about synthetic content in fashion advertising. Continues to be referenced in ongoing coverage of Demna's second collection this week; outside 14-day freshness window but included as the highest-tier anchor for the still-live AI-backlash critical thread.
